assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mesoporous nanocrystalline TiO2 films sensitised with molecular dyes turned a materials-architecture idea into a new photovoltaic principle. Clear, original and widely adopted; it founded a field of molecular and hybrid photovoltaics and is a textbook case of structure (nanoporous film, interface) determining function.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the decisive contribution, with Grätzel the sustained intellectual driver of the field. Hagfeldt is a major later contributor to mechanism and devices, but his role is less decisive for the founding discovery; a two-person prize fits the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent confirmation and commercial and academic use. Recognition is clearly timely, if not overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to include Hagfeldt or other contributors to dye design.
Commercial efficiency has been overtaken by perovskites, which could be read as reducing practical impact, though the conceptual influence remains.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves, via organic structure-directing agents, new framework types and site-isolated active centres, underpins refining, petrochemicals and emissions control. Enormous industrial and scientific impact, and a field I know closely from structure solution of new zeolites.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design and application), Davis (organic templating and new frameworks, molecular-sieve catalysis) and Zones (SDA design, commercial zeolites such as SSZ-13) form a plausible trio. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are important but more specialised or later. The candidate is broad, so the prize wording would need care.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation. Industrial use is established. Recognition would be timely, but the area is diffuse and credit is spread over many groups.
uncertainties: The candidate is broad, and the specific discovery being rewarded is not sharply defined.
Individual contributions are hard to separate from Barrer and Breck-era foundations and from industrial work.
I cannot independently verify the exact credit split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and polyhedra gives well-defined, crystallographically characterised hollow architectures with host-guest chemistry, catalysis in confined spaces and sensing. Original and conceptually clear, and closely related to framework chemistry that the committee has recently recognised.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (Pd2L4 and M6L4 cages, defined cavities, crystalline sponge), Raymond (tetrahedral M4L6 cages and encapsulated reactivity) and Stang (coordination-driven self-assembly of polygons and polyhedra) are the natural trio. Nitschke and Ward are important but later. Fujita is arguably the strongest single claim.
assessment.maturity: Structures are firmly established by crystallography and NMR, with decades of independent work. Timing is reasonable, but the overlap with the recent framework-materials prize could count either for or against.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a sufficiently distinct discovery from the recently recognised framework chemistry.
Practical applications are less mature than the structural science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allows structure determination from nano- and microcrystals and time-resolved studies of reactions, beating radiation-damage limits. It is an enabling method that lets a community see what it could not before, and it resonates with my own work on small crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the XFEL demonstrations and methodology, Fromme developed membrane-protein nanocrystal sample handling and the early experiments, and Hajdu proposed the diffraction-before-destruction concept and the biological case. Schlichting is also strong, so the choice of three is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Methodology is validated across many facilities and systems, but the number of landmark structures and routine users is still modest compared with synchrotrons and cryo-EM. Recognition is plausible but possibly early.
uncertainties: Whether the chemical (rather than structural-biology) impact is large enough.
Contested choice among Chapman, Fromme, Hajdu and Schlichting.
Facility access limits breadth of adoption.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts reframe heterogeneous catalysis as atom-efficient, well-defined active sites on supports, linked to atomic-resolution STEM and X-ray absorption evidence. Strong conceptual and application appeal, and I am sympathetic to the microscopy-enabled structural evidence.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Qiao, Wang, Liu, Zhang and Li paper coined and popularised the concept; Zhang led the group, Qiao was first author and Liu supplied the electron microscopy. Earlier single-atom precedents (e.g. Flytzani-Stephanopoulos work on atomically dispersed species) may complicate credit, though that name is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: The field is large and active but still debating site definition, stability under reaction conditions and the actual proportion of active single atoms. Possibly premature.
uncertainties: Priority and novelty versus earlier atomically dispersed catalysts.
Many claimed single-atom structures rely on limited local evidence.
Industrial-scale impact is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a very rapid rise in solar cell efficiency, with strong materials-chemistry content (defect tolerance, composition engineering). The impact on photovoltaics research is very large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park and Snaith made the key solid-state advances in 2012. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also contributed, so credit is diffuse and disputed, and Grätzel could be better placed in the dye-sensitised candidate.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is confirmed independently, but long-term operational stability, lead toxicity and scale-up remain unresolved, so the technology may not yet be mature enough.
uncertainties: Stability and toxicity could reduce lasting impact.
Contested allocation among at least six credited people.
Possible overlap with the dye-sensitised candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structures of nitrogenase, including the FeMo cofactor with its interstitial carbide, and mechanistic work on the catalytic cycle address one of the most important and demanding problems in bioinorganic chemistry, biological nitrogen fixation.
assessment.attribution: Rees and colleagues solved the MoFe protein and cofactor structures, Einsle resolved the central carbide, and Seefeldt contributed mechanistic and spectroscopic understanding. Dean and Ribbe are also significant, so a three-person limit forces difficult exclusions.
assessment.maturity: The structure is well established and independently confirmed, but the actual mechanism of N2 reduction is still debated, so the prize rationale should focus on structure.
uncertainties: Catalytic mechanism and the E4 state remain only partly understood.
Credit is spread over five people, and structural versus mechanistic roles differ.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carbon nanotubes, especially single-walled nanotubes, opened a major family of nanocarbon materials with exceptional properties and wide study, and were characterised by electron microscopy, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Iijima's 1991 observation was decisive for multiwalled nanotubes, and the 1993 single-walled work by Iijima and Bethune (independently) was decisive for SWNTs. Endo's earlier work on carbon fibres complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, but commercial impact has been modest relative to expectations and the Nobel timing may be late or fall in the physics domain.
uncertainties: Priority disputes with earlier carbon filament observations.
Whether the discovery is judged chemistry or physics.
